subject: social-studies
title: Philosophical Foundations of Civic Society and Government
essential_question: How can a government protect individual rights and pursue the common good at the same time?
topics: unalienable rights and the common good
forms and limits of political authority
performance_task: Design and defend a governance framework that balances rights and the common good, citing foundational arguments accurately.
anchor_sources: Declaration of Independence (National Archives)
Constitution of the United States (National Archives)
The Federalist Papers (Avalon Project)

subject: social-studies
title: Founding and Development of American Government
essential_question: How do Democratic Values and Constitutional Principles work together, and where do they collide?
topics: influential speeches, writings, cases, and laws
performance_task: Trace one Democratic Value from a founding document through a later case or law, citing each source accurately.
anchor_sources: The Federalist Papers (Avalon Project)
Anti-Federalist essays, including the Brutus and Federal Farmer letters (Library of Congress digital collections)
Bill of Rights (National Archives)
Declaration of Sentiments, 1848 (Library of Congress)

subject: social-studies
title: Structure and Function of Governments in the United States
essential_question: How do the branches and levels of American government compete and cooperate to make policy?
topics: the legislative branch and the power of the purse
the executive branch and the federal bureaucracy
the judicial branch and judicial review
federalism and the division of powers
state, local, and tribal governments, revenue, and direct democracy
parties, media, interest groups, and other civic actors
performance_task: Trace one policy from proposal to implementation across branches and levels of government, documenting each step, its funding source, and the civic actors who shaped it.
anchor_sources: Constitution of the United States, Articles I-III (National Archives)
Constitution of the State of Michigan, 1963 (Michigan Legislature)
Congressional and state legislative records (congress.gov and legislature.mi.gov)

subject: social-studies
title: Rights and Liberties in the United States
essential_question: When may government limit a right, and who decides?
topics: application of the Bill of Rights
extensions of civil rights and civil liberties
tensions among liberty, order, and equality
limits on rights and their justification
performance_task: Analyze a rights conflict using the constitutional text, the reasoning of decided cases, and at least two fairly represented positions.
anchor_sources: Bill of Rights and the Fourteenth Amendment (National Archives)
Published opinions of the Supreme Court of the United States (supremecourt.gov and Library of Congress)
Civil Rights Act of 1964 (National Archives)

subject: social-studies
title: The United States in World Affairs and Citizenship in Action
essential_question: How do citizens and institutions shape what the United States does at home and abroad?
topics: formation and implementation of United States foreign policy
the United States role in international institutions and affairs
rights and responsibilities in civic society
civic inquiry, public policy, civic action, and public discourse
performance_task: Complete the civics performance task: a public-issue analysis with a documented, lawful, and feasible civic action plan.
anchor_sources: Charter of the United Nations, 1945 (United Nations Digital Library)
Immigration and Nationality Act and naturalization requirements (U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services)
Federal Register rules and notices (federalregister.gov) and public rulemaking dockets (regulations.gov)

subject: social-studies
title: The Market Economy: Scarcity, Decisions, and Competition
essential_question: How do scarcity and incentives shape the choices households and businesses make?
performance_task: Model a real decision with explicit opportunity costs, marginal analysis, and cited data.
anchor_sources: Bureau of Labor Statistics data series (bls.gov)
Federal Reserve Economic Data series (fred.stlouisfed.org)

subject: social-studies
title: Prices, Markets, and the Role of Government
essential_question: What happens to prices, quantities, and people when government acts in a market?
performance_task: Analyze one government action in a market, showing predicted effects on price, quantity, and different households.
anchor_sources: Consumer Price Index and producer price series (bls.gov)
Federal budget and tax documents (U.S. Government Publishing Office, govinfo.gov)

subject: social-studies
title: The National Economy
essential_question: What do national economic indicators actually tell us, and what do they hide?
performance_task: Interpret a set of real economic indicators and defend a claim about national economic conditions, naming the limits of each measure.
anchor_sources: Gross domestic product and national accounts (Bureau of Economic Analysis, bea.gov)
Employment situation and price index releases (bls.gov)
Federal Open Market Committee statements (federalreserve.gov)

subject: social-studies
title: The International Economy and Personal Finance
essential_question: How do global markets and personal financial choices affect each other?
topics: exchange rates, tariffs, and trade barriers
performance_task: Complete the course capstone: a two-part defense pairing an economic policy analysis with a personal financial decision model.
anchor_sources: International trade statistics (census.gov and United Nations Digital Library)
Consumer financial disclosure and education materials (Consumer Financial Protection Bureau, consumerfinance.gov)
